facts.text: Grelton was founded in 1881 when the Cloverleaf Railroad arrived, and its name honored landowner Alexander Grelle, dropping one 'l' from the original spelling.
The town sits at the four‑corner junction of Monroe, Richfield, Harrison, and Damascus townships, a crossroads that helped it grow.
Early economy was driven by timber; sawmills and barrel‑stave factories processed oak, walnut, and poplar for Canadian shipbuilders.
The Grelton Cemetery, started in 1893 on a five‑acre Noah Jackson donation, now spans 40 acres and hosts walking paths.
A veterans memorial in the cemetery honors local military service, reflecting the community’s long‑standing patriotism.
